newsitem.title: USA: Mobil to expand Speedpass gasoline marketing.
newsitem.headline: Mobil to expand Speedpass gasoline marketing.

text.p: Mobil Corp on Wednesday said it planned to introduce its Mobil Speedpass pay-at-the-pump technology at service stations in key markets across the United States this year.

Customers enrolled in the Speedpass program are able purchase gasoline by waving miniature electronic devices attached to their key chains in front of designated gasoline pumps. No credit cards or cash are required to complete the purchase.
Initially, the company's goal is to distribute one million Speedpass key tags to customers who sign up for the service.
Similar to the electronic tags used to reduce waiting time at highway toll booths, Speedpass is a proprietary technology that employs radio signals.
During a six-month trial in St. Louis, customers said they appreciated the increased speed and simplicity of buying gasoline with the Speedpass system, Mobil said.

In April, Mobil will introduce Speedpass in those markets where it has high-tech service stations, including the Northeast, Los Angeles and Phoenix. Six hundred outlets have already signed up, and more than 1,000 sites are expected to have the technology by the end of 1997, Baker said.
"Our research tells us that customers are looking for the fastest and easiest way to fill up," said Brian Baker,

"We answered this need in 1986 by pioneering pay-at-the-pump technology that allows customers to use credit cards right at the pump," he said. "Mobil Speedpass simplifies the process even more, making gasoline buying even faster.

The technology opens the way for transponder devices that can be affixed to a vehicle and automatically read when it pulls up to a gasoline pump. Such devices might also be able to determine when a vehicle requires an oil change, tune-up or other services.
Baker said Speedpasses tags could be deactivated quickly by calling a 1-800 number should they be lost or stolen.
Speedpass uses the Texas Instruments Registration and Identification System (TIRIS), a technology for identifying radio frequencies.
The Wayne Division of Dresser Industries Inc made the integrated retail fueling systems.
